newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' 92-day T-bill rate at 11.172 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' 92-day T-bill rate at 11.172 pct.

text.p: The Philippines' benchmark 92-day Treasury bill rate fell to 11.172 percent from 11.679 percent registered in the previous auction, the Bureau of Treasury said on Monday.
The auction committee did not hold an auction last Monday since the market was closed for a national holiday.
Tenders for the 92-day bills totalled 6.625 billion pesos, but only 1.0 billion pesos worth of bids were accepted by the committee.
Instead of the usual 91-day maturity, the auction committee had to add one day because the 91st day falls on a national holiday.
The 182-day bill rate fell to 11.405 percent from the previous auction's 11.931 percent, while the 364-day bills fell to 11.8 percent from 12.455 percent.
Bankers attributed the sharp drop in the auction rates to the influx of fresh funds which were released due to the one percentage point reduction in the banks' reserve requirements.
The six-month and one-year bills were over-subscribed. Financial institutions tendered 13.345 billion pesos for the six-month bills and 18.4 billion pesos for the one-year bills.
The committee accepted only 1.5 billion pesos for the six-month bills, and 2.0 billion pesos for the one-year bills.
